header.name: Chan Shun-Chih
header.title: AI-Native Software Engineer · Senior Systems Analyst
header.summary: Four years of Python backend and AI application engineering. With a spec-driven, AI-agent workflow (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI) I deliver enterprise systems, Text-to-SQL and SRE triage systems, ML models, cloud IaC and consumer products solo — then institutionalize the workflow (Claude Skills with evals, tiered subagent dispatch) and build tooling for it (a self-built MCP Gateway, Claude Code mods). Previously led two AI video products to 7,000+ users, halving monthly cost and cutting failure rate from 30% to under 1%. JLPT N1.

positioning.title: Ship products with AI
positioning.body: Enterprise projects plus six live side projects, all in the git history: Text-to-SQL from PoC to production, an SRE triage agent built solo in 5 weeks, a job scheduler with 1,190 tests in a day, a ramen map live on day one.

positioning.title: Manage how AI works
positioning.body: Spec first, TDD, an AI code-review loop; design phases produce documents only, subagents implement after decisions are final; decisions by eval — a 65-case evaluation rejected a model upgrade in favor of precedent override, 12% → 80%.

positioning.title: Build tools for AI
positioning.body: A self-built MCP Gateway, Claude Skills with evals, Claude Code mods; boundaries for AI agents: proposal-only changes gated by tests, zero shell and zero cloud permissions, never silently dropping a query condition.

experience.company: IT subsidiary of a retail group
experience.intro: Cloud architecture, batch and data platforms, AI application development and operations, spanning cloud architecture, DevOps, data engineering and AI products.

groups.name: Retail CDP: batch platform evolution (ADF polling → queue → job scheduler)
bullets: Replaced a 15-minute ADF polling job with a .NET BackgroundService + Azure Storage Queue pipeline: global sp_getapplock claiming, heartbeat lease renewal, poison queue + failure notifications, recovery scan as a safety net; claim latency 15 min → seconds; led the production cutover after a rehearsal in test that surfaced trigger-branch and storage-firewall issues in advance

Hardened it after three incidents: Run From Package to end deployment races, streamed download lists to fix a 6.64M-member OOM, second-level graceful handoff on restart instead of a 60-minute zombie reclaim, transient-error retry on SQL connections

Designed and implemented a second-generation job scheduler (dev complete, production pending): one job table for six task types, one applock per resource, every state transition a conditional update checked by affected rows, DB-clock timeouts, scale-out and concurrency by table values without redeploys; retires three ADF chains and the Storage Queue; 710-line spec, 1,190 unit tests, 68/68 dev integration tests; fixed cross-instance races and a cross-thread connection deadlock

Working method: design phases produce documents only (spec plus ~40 briefs/reviews); after decisions, subagents implement (sonnet for simple tasks, opus for SQL/concurrency) with a review per task; 88 commits in one day
groups.lead: ADF 15-minute polling → Storage Queue → single-table job scheduler; led the production cutover, hardened after three incidents, gen-2 with 1,190 unit tests

groups.name: Retail CDP: SQL builder rewrite and performance root-causing
bullets: Rewrote Razor-template SQL assembly as a parameterized C# SqlBuilder (four box types) and fixed three known bugs; ran a Synapse parameterization PoC first (multi-statement CTAS, temp-table visibility, TOP(@var), string parameter typing) which decided a DECLARE fallback; implemented by Copilot over 15 TDD tasks with Claude reviewing in batches

Three measurement-first root-cause investigations with zero builder changes: NVARCHAR implicit conversion killing an index seek on 82.7M rows → CONVERT on the parameter side, 559s → 0.4s; stale production view definition in dev → one box 1237s → 12.5s and a full smoke run 24m45s → 47s; appsettings.json never deployed due to a csproj setting → three 3600s timeouts became a 5.7-minute run, with the default fixed to prevent recurrence

Dashboard contract revision in production (three-parameter SPs, dashboard computed in the same message after packaging, replacing ADF dispatch), SP bucket completion so zero-purchase packages pass validation; materialized reused CTEs as CTAS temp tables: largest package 12.6M members 425/364s → 141/131s with row-identical output across four sizes
groups.lead: Razor SQL assembly → parameterized builder; three measurement-first root-causes: 559s → 0.4s, full run 24m45s → 47s, zero builder changes

groups.name: Retail CDP: Text-to-SQL (PoC → production)
bullets: PoC v1 on synthetic data + DuckDB; PoC v2 against a production replica (920M transaction rows): understand → value-linking guards → option-based clarification (≤3 rounds) → echo understanding → generate SQL → sql_guard validation and auto-repair → EXPLAIN gate → execute → code computes statistics, the LLM only interprets

Production: standalone FastAPI service; sqlglot AST dialect packs for both T-SQL and PostgreSQL; semantic-model YAML where every fact carries confidence / evidence / review; 10 ADRs; data profiling 650s → 338s

Evaluation suite: gold-SQL numeric comparison (0.5% tolerance) 10/10, behavior tests (should ask / should not ask / cannot do) 23/23 × 2, insight fabrication check at zero, actionability 3.3 → 4.17; Claude vs GPT comparison (deeper conclusions vs ~100× cost)

Product-positioning ADR: once two more systems were confirmed to onboard, pivoted from a single-system tool to "execution engine + 13-step onboarding process"; guard rule: any condition that cannot become SQL must be asked back, never silently dropped
groups.lead: Natural-language queries over 920M rows, PoC → production FastAPI service; gold SQL 10/10, behavior tests 23/23, zero fabrication

groups.name: SRE-agent: Azure Data Factory failure-triage system (designed and built solo, ~5 weeks)
bullets: Read-only across 3 ADF factories / 44 pipelines: every 5 minutes detect failed runs → de-duplicate into incidents (failure chains, soft-failure detection) → classify with rules first, LLM as fallback, unclassified on failure → Teams Adaptive Card to the on-call engineer (conclusion / what to do now / what to check first); ~9,900 lines Python, 208 tests, 140 incidents
Rule engine with patterns, an actions allowlist and playbooks all in YAML, hot-reloaded every cycle; the LLM (Azure OpenAI, switchable to Claude) is called only when no rule matches (~3% of cases)

Used evals to reject a model upgrade: on 65 cases rules 12% / gpt-mini 46% / Opus 83%, but after removing duplicates the two models tied → the bottleneck was rule actions, not the model → built human-precedent override instead; action accuracy 12% → 80%, act/don't-act 25% → 92%; daily digest cut noise 53% with zero misses

Learning agent (Claude Opus on Microsoft Foundry) is proposal-only: a human clicks apply on the site, pytest runs automatically and reverts on failure, passing changes auto-commit; tools limited to reading the DB and knowledge files, commenting and proposing — zero shell, zero Azure permissions
Streamlit on-call site (with /mobile), supervisor guarding three processes plus a watchdog, SQLite / Azure Table dual storage, archive of 73,292 historical ADF runs
groups.lead: Read-only ADF failure triage, built solo in ~5 weeks; evals rejected a model upgrade, precedent override took accuracy 12% → 80%

groups.name: Retail allocation platform
bullets: Independently delivered an enterprise retail allocation platform (1,100+ files) in 2.5 months with AI collaboration; heavy requirements interviews, allocation logic designed from per-store sales data and special cases

Backend Python 3.12 / FastAPI / SQLAlchemy 2 / Alembic / PostgreSQL in a layered architecture (api / core / engine / etl / repositories / services); frontend React 19 + TypeScript / Vite / TanStack Query·Table·Virtual / react-hook-form + zod / Tailwind 4
Contract-first: openapi.json → openapi-typescript generates frontend types, keeping both sides in sync
CI/CD on Azure Pipelines: PRs run backend pytest and frontend lint/test/build in parallel; 8 backend test modules, 56 frontend test files, UAT smoke tests

Requirement alignment via single-file HTML prototypes that stakeholders preview before real development, cutting the spec → build → acceptance cycle; disciplined docs (decisions / lessons / runbooks / roadmap)
groups.lead: Enterprise allocation system (1,100+ files) delivered solo in 2.5 months; FastAPI + React 19, contract-first, Azure Pipelines CI/CD

groups.name: Demand-allocation ML models
bullets: Store-level allocation forecasting with LightGBM, CatBoost, Optuna tuning and isotonic calibration
Systematic pipeline: baseline → feature engineering → ablation → blending → rules overlay → misallocation diagnosis; delivered ML allocation plan draft, ER model and table schema
groups.lead: Store-level allocation forecasting with LightGBM / CatBoost, Optuna tuning, systematic experiments (baseline → ablation → blending)

groups.name: Enterprise Customer Data Platform (6 repos / 2,200+ files): AI API and foundations
bullets: React 19 + TS + TanStack Router/Query frontend, .NET Web API, .NET batch system with unit tests; SQL Server multi-schema design + Azure Synapse warehouse (CTAS / HASH-distributed tuning)

AI API: Python 3.13 + FastAPI + Google ADK agent pipeline + LiteLLM → Azure OpenAI; automated product tagging (migrated from a legacy service) and a 3-stage marketing-copy pipeline; strict API contract (four status codes, per-user rate limiting, fail-honestly-no-fallback)
Three environments (dev/test/prod) per repo on Azure DevOps pipelines; incident records and architecture runbooks; legacy-service retirement and a production misconfiguration incident
groups.lead: A 6-repo CDP: React + .NET + Synapse; AI API on a Google ADK pipeline for product tagging and marketing copy

groups.name: MCP Gateway (self-built AI infrastructure)
bullets: Wraps internal HTTP APIs as MCP tools so Claude Code / Codex / Copilot reach internal systems through one secure entry point; tool catalog in DB, approved tools go live without code changes or restarts
Security: per-client Bearer auth, SSRF protection (blocks localhost/cloud metadata + allowlist), Fernet-encrypted upstream credentials, audit logs with sensitive-parameter masking
Python 3.12 / MCP SDK (Streamable HTTP) / Starlette / SQLAlchemy 2 / Streamlit admin; 20+ test files incl. acceptance tests (pytest-asyncio + respx); v1 live in 3 days
Extensions: response bodies added to the audit log (UTF-8-safe truncation with original byte count), a connect page generating configs for eight AI clients, a per-client → per-user permission draft
groups.lead: Live in 3 days: internal APIs wrapped as MCP tools with per-client auth, SSRF protection, encrypted credentials, input/output audit

groups.name: Convenience-store auto-ordering system: operations documentation
bullets: Wrote a 10-section onboarding plan for engineers new to the system: inventory of 183 ADF pipelines (39 without triggers), 66 triggers, a 1,324-line core SP; risk register (single maintainer, plaintext SAS, no test environment, global temp tables) and a four-week learning path

Daily-dispatch runbook: timing of five main stages with latest start times, a parallel emergency path, a decision tree; key insight that ML timeout plus retry can stall 8 hours without an error, so decisions must be time-based (09:30 checkpoint) rather than alert-driven; BlobFuse upgrade investigation, ML pipeline retry / webhook design proposal
groups.lead: Onboarding plan and daily-dispatch runbook for an auto-ordering system; inventoried 183 pipelines and a 1,324-line core SP

groups.name: Log anomaly analysis
bullets: Gradio UI with two-stage filtering of large logs → Azure OpenAI analysis → SQLite; strict three-layer decoupling (filter / ai / db); token and cost estimation before each AI call with threshold warnings
groups.lead: Gradio two-stage filtering → Azure OpenAI analysis → SQLite; token and cost estimate before every AI call

groups.name: Enterprise chatbot product deployment
bullets: Source governance and dockerization of an enterprise chatbot product (Java/JSP/Kotlin, 700+ files): Compose with MSSQL 2022, Redis Stack, Solr 9.5, custom parser; DB init, health checks, fresh-VM deployment SOP; git filter-repo history cleanup, Git LFS; production and UAT upgrades (including training a colleague), OOM / WSL incident handling
groups.lead: Dockerized a Java enterprise chatbot (700+ files) with a deployment SOP; production and UAT upgrades, incident handling

groups.name: Azure IaC, security & data engineering
bullets: Modular Bicep IaC (network / keyvault / storage / postgres / appservice): IP allowlist + Private Endpoint dual path, Key Vault secrets, VNet Integration + RBAC, rollback docs

Reconciled IaC with portal drift: what-if reports "no change" for resources with listKeys() and runtime references → az show diffs per resource plus activity-log tracing; kept existing RBAC assignment GUIDs to avoid duplicate guid() resources; crontab lost on App Service Linux restarts → startup script re-registers schedules
Dify (open-source LLM platform) on Azure Container Apps (PostgreSQL + pgvector / Redis / Storage, with cost estimate); Terraform for LLM resource groups
Post-quantum crypto asset scanner M0: inventory across TLS / Key Vault / App Service / App Gateway with algorithm, key size, expiry and quantum-risk grade (NIST FIPS 203/204/205)
groups.lead: Modular Bicep IaC, reconciled with portal drift, Dify on Container Apps, a post-quantum crypto asset scanner

groups.name: AI engineering methodology (institutionalized)
bullets: One shared AGENTS.md driving Claude Code and Copilot CLI on enterprise projects; git worktree for parallel branches
Adopted and operated the agent-skill toolchain and built an automated AI code-review loop (AI fixes → commit → replies to review thread → re-review until it converges)
Packaged team domain knowledge as Claude Skills with evals (Azure Synapse tuning, ADF standards) plus project-specific skills (e.g. an Azure DevOps PR flow)

A self-made dispatch skill routes each task to the cheapest model that is good enough (haiku to find / sonnet for well-specified work / opus for cross-file and concurrency); a self-made Claude Code mod, context-bar, shows context usage, token cost and rate limits live
Internal tech talk on the requirement → AI prototype → user alignment → build workflow (14-page outline, script, 4 diagrams) with 5 reusable de-projectized skills
groups.lead: Dual-agent AGENTS.md, AI code-review loop, Claude Skills with evals, dispatch skill and context-bar mod, internal talks

bullets: Led OVideo, an AI-driven content-to-video platform serving 1,800+ users, incl. membership, subscriptions, payment integration and Azure deployment

Designed the full video-generation pipeline: LLMs (GPT-4, Claude, Gemini) for content analysis, scripting and image-text matching; FFmpeg for processing, subtitles and encoding; async tasks with Server-Sent Events progress

Performance and cost: parallelized the pipeline to cut average generation time from 30 to 15 minutes (-50%); re-architected Azure services to halve monthly infrastructure cost (NT$40,000 → NT$20,000); serverless architecture scaled capacity from 10 to 100+ concurrent users; 1,100+ videos processed
Introduced Clean Architecture, cutting new-feature development time by 50%; designed a PostgreSQL / MongoDB hybrid for high concurrency

Built Osense AI, a LINE-based AI avatar and voice-cloning system (5,400+ users): lip-sync and voice cloning, full LINE Bot user flows; fixed upstream open-source bugs and error handling to cut failure rate from 30% to under 1%
Rapid PoCs with Gradio and light frontends for client demos; introduced AI tooling to speed up development
experience.lead: Led two AI video / avatar products (7,000+ users): generation time -50%, monthly cost -50%, failure rate 30% → <1%

bullets: Built internal web systems with Django: table design from requirements interviews, API and flow planning; Django + jQuery integration with GitLab CI/CD
Developed and maintained scrapers with Selenium and Requests; optimized existing scrapers and anti-bot handling
Built a PDF invoice extraction tool that captures key fields into the database, reducing manual entry to a field check
Introduced GitLab version control and a basic development process; applied the Repository Pattern to isolate data access
experience.lead: Django internal systems, scrapers and a PDF invoice extractor, introduced GitLab CI/CD

sideProjects.name: menmap (麵咩撲) — Taipei ramen map
sideProjects.desc: Daily automated Google Maps harvesting (scheduled on a home machine, dual backends requests + Playwright, per-shop diff against the last snapshot) → D1 + static JSON; MapLibre map, open-now / metro / style filters, a "where today" dice, self-written Google OAuth (HS256 JWT HttpOnly), ramen diary / friends / lists, PWA, Worker-rendered SEO pages + schema.org; LLM (Claude Sonnet on Foundry) classified 491 shops into 15 ramen styles for US$2.5. ~24,000 lines Python + TS, 21 D1 tables, ~58 Worker routes, Playwright e2e. Day one's 34 commits already included the pipeline, map, API and the production domain; 130 commits in 15 days. Decisions: rejected Google Places API (US$70–90/month) after a 14-minute estimate; proved datacenter IPs get degraded responses → scraper stays home; fixed a D1 read-quota blowout with edge caching and scoped SQL. $0 a month.
sideProjects.lead: Taipei ramen map, live on day one; daily harvesting, D1, LLM classification, Worker-rendered SEO pages; $0 a month

sideProjects.name: pachipachi (ぱちぱち) — Japanese typing trainer
sideProjects.desc: Romaji input judged key by key into kana (pure-TS engine: longest-match tokenizer, っ/ん rules, state machine, score = kpm × accuracy², replay); kana charts → N5–N1 vocabulary 500 / sentences 100 / business letters / net slang, 40 lessons, 27 timed leaderboards; practice your own lyrics synced to YouTube (kuromoji kanji→kana in the browser, zero external APIs on the Worker). SvelteKit 2 + Svelte 5 + Drizzle + D1/KV + Better Auth; pnpm workspace. 62 commits, ~26,000 lines and 470 tests in 3 working days; 7 worktree subagents developed in parallel and merged the same day. Server recomputes scores from the client key log plus 6 anticheat rules; lyrics-copyright design (researched JASRAC and Taiwan copyright law art. 90-4: shared timelines store only per-line SHA-256, notice-and-takedown, three strikes).
sideProjects.lead: Japanese typing trainer in 3 working days with 470 tests; pure-TS kana engine, server-side anticheat, lyrics-copyright design

sideProjects.name: Career Agent — AI job-search assistant
sideProjects.desc: Upload résumé → AI diagnosis → crawl listings → semantic fit ranking (score + reasons + missing skills) → tailored cover letters → application board; curl_cffi Chrome TLS fingerprint to pass the job site's WAF, two-stage throttling, Google login + daily quota, LLM provider abstraction. Local edition career-sentinel: reads the logged-in job-site session (rebrowser-playwright), a tool-use "job-search commander" chat agent, interview prep, salary insights, token accounting; the agent never writes to the job site. FastAPI + MongoDB + Claude API; React + TS + Mantine; 543 commits, 252 tests; backend on Cloud Run. 10K+ views on the launch post, real users.
sideProjects.lead: AI job-search assistant: diagnosis → crawl → fit ranking → cover letters; 543 commits, 10K+ post views, real users

sideProjects.name: Loka Note — housing decision tool
sideProjects.desc: Address-level reports: commute (TDX bus/metro + OSM road-graph Dijkstra for scooter/car), rent and sale transaction-price benchmarks, mortgage and monthly cost, amenities (OSM Overpass), hazards (flood / liquefaction), crime (police theft data), garbage-truck routes, YouBike; favorites board and comparison table; period-based paid plans with entitlements. React 19 + TanStack + Hono + D1 + Drizzle, Zod shared across client and server, Vitest in two runtimes (workerd / Node); ~23,000 lines TS, 138 commits over 10 development days. Product pivot driven by legal risk: after reviewing fair-trade rulings, stopped scraping listing sites — users bring their own listings and the product sells only the analysis layer built on commercially usable open data.
sideProjects.lead: Address-to-report housing decisions: commute, prices, hazards, crime; pivoted off listing scraping over legal risk

sideProjects.name: Suancui (酸脆) — Threads AI roast generator
sideProjects.desc: Viral-loop design (share to unlock hidden styles); TypeScript npm-workspaces monorepo: React frontend, Cloudflare Workers + Hono + KV, swappable scraping layer (self-hosted GraphQL crawler / third-party API fallback); four packages each with vitest tests; anti-fabrication and anti-harassment guardrails. 67 commits in one day.
sideProjects.lead: Threads AI roast generator, 67 commits in a day; Workers + Hono + KV, viral loop and anti-fabrication guardrails

sideProjects.name: iThome Ironman 2023: Django source-code deep dive
sideProjects.desc: A 30-day series tracing Django internals from everyday commands and APIs into request handling, the ORM and middleware.
sideProjects.lead: A 30-day Django internals series: request flow, ORM, middleware

sideProjects.name: Other
sideProjects.desc: Real-time bus Android widget PoC (Flutter + native Kotlin background service + TDX; 30/30 per-minute updates on a real device); Lootfall (Godot 4 roguelite M0–M5 plus a web idle edition in one day); Kapp Korean flashcards (Flutter + SM-2, two days); daily work-log system (Flask, 62 tests, one day); reverse-engineered an undocumented Central Weather Administration API; personal RAG agent (chromadb); 56+ posts on a Hexo tech blog.
sideProjects.lead: Bus widget PoC, Godot roguelite, Flutter flashcards, daily work-log, weather-API reverse engineering, RAG agent, 56+ blog posts
